cards.headline: Same price. Two completely different charts.
cards.body: Two stocks both trade at $50 today. One stepped up there from $30. The other slid there from $80. The price is identical. The structure is not, and structure is the part you can actually read.

cards.headline: An uptrend is higher highs and higher lows.
cards.body: Price never moves in a straight line. It pushes up, pulls back, pushes up again. When each push tops **above** the last top, and each pullback bottoms **above** the last bottom, that sequence is an uptrend.

cards.title: An uptrend, point by point
cards.caption: Highs step up: 112, 124, 138, 152. Lows step up too: 106, 116, 129. Both sequences rising at once — that is the entire definition.

cards.prompt: A stock's last three pullback lows were 40, 44, then 43. Highs kept rising throughout. Is the uptrend intact?

options.label: Yes — the highs are still rising

cards.explanation: An uptrend needs **both** sequences. The moment a low prints under the previous low, the higher-low chain has stopped, whatever the highs did.

cards.headline: A downtrend is the same rule, inverted.
cards.body: Lower highs and lower lows. Each rally stops **below** the last rally. Each drop bottoms **below** the last bottom. A downtrend does not mean the company is failing. It means sellers keep meeting buyers at lower prices.

cards.title: A range: neither one
cards.caption: Ten sessions. No high above 52, no low under 48. The tops do not climb and the bottoms do not fall — so there is no sequence to name.

cards.body: Every chart sits in one of three states at any moment. Naming the state is the first thing you do, before anything else.

cards.headline: Trend describes the past, not the future.
cards.body: A trend is a label for what price has already done. It carries no promise about tomorrow. Charts spend long stretches in neither trend, and a range is exactly where {{strategy:trend-following|trend following}} logic performs worst.

cards.title: Where the sequence breaks
cards.caption: Lows climb 110, 124, 139 — then print 133. That 133 is the first low to sit under the one before it. The chain ends there.

cards.body: An uptrend is usually called broken at the first lower [[1]] — a pullback that finishes under the previous pullback.
cards.explanation: A lower high on its own is only a warning. The lower **low** is the event most definitions use, because it is the first thing the earlier structure said would not happen.

cards.headline: Broken is a rule you set in advance.
cards.body: The chart never announces a break. You pick the definition — a lower low, a close under an average, a fixed percentage — and you pick it before you are watching. Choose it afterwards and you will choose whatever just happened.

cards.title: Trend and structure
cards.summary: Trend is a description of the sequence of highs and lows. It is not a forecast.
bullets: Uptrend: higher highs and higher lows. Downtrend: the mirror.
A range is neither, and charts sit in one often.
The break is the first lower low after a run of higher lows.
You define broken in advance. The chart will not do it for you.

cards.insight: A trend is a sentence about what already happened. The market is under no obligation to finish it the way you would.
